verdict.rationale: PostHog's feature-flag docs state that person properties (attribute-based rules), cohorts (reusable segments), and groups determine who matches a release condition, and that flags can be rolled out by percentage. The evidence is a single summary line, though, and it does not show per-variation targeting, so coverage is partial rather than complete. missing for 10: evidence of multivariate flags with per-variant targeting, detail on rule operators and combinations, independent or hands-on corroboration of cohort-based targeting.

support.subject: As a developer, I can target flags with attribute-based rules and reusable segments so the right users see the right variation

citations.quote: Person properties, cohorts, and groups decide who matches a release condition.
Create flags, set release conditions, schedule changes, and watch rollouts land.
Wrap a change in a flag, roll it out to 1% of users, watch what happens, and turn it off the moment something looks wrong
